curatorBrief.title: Welcome to Letter-Sound Group 3!
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome Kindergarteners to six exciting new letter sounds: g, o, u, l, f, and b, while celebrating and practicing all 13 previously learned sounds from Group 1 and Group 2 for a full cumulative 19-letter adventure.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Introduce the new sounds /g/, /ŏ/, /ŭ/, /l/, /f/, /b/ while reviewing all 13 previous sounds (s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d). Practice problems must pull from the full 19-letter cumulative list.

components.title: Meet New Letter Friends: g, o, u, l, f, b
components.intent: Present clear, picture-supported cards introducing each new letter in Group 3 alongside its key sound: g (/g/ as in gift), o (/ŏ/ as in octopus), u (/ŭ/ as in umbrella), l (/l/ as in lion), f (/f/ as in fan), and b (/b/ as in bat).

components.title: Find the Letters: Group 3 & Cumulative Review
components.intent: Engage kindergarten students in visual discrimination and letter recognition across the cumulative 19-letter set (Group 3: g, o, u, l, f, b plus previous groups), searching for uppercase/lowercase forms and spotting initial letters in engaging spoken prompts.

components.title: Sound and Blend with New Letters
components.intent: Let students tap letter tiles to hear sounds for the newly introduced letters (g, o, u, l, f, b) and blend them with review letters to form simple, decodable CVC words such as 'fog', 'bug', 'leg', and 'sun'.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Independently produce the most common sound for each letter in this cumulative set, when shown its grapheme. Assess without first saying its sound: s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d, g, o, u, l, f, b.

components.title: Speak the Continuous Sounds
components.intent: Direct Instruction live-judged practice focusing on producing continuous stretchable sounds and short vowels from the cumulative set (/f/, /l/, /ŏ/, /ŭ/, along with review sounds /s/, /m/, /n/, /r/) directly when seeing each grapheme.

components.title: Say the Sound & Link the Letter
components.intent: Conduct live direct instruction assessment where the grapheme is displayed cold and the student independently produces the sound or selects the matching letter for stops and vowels across the full 19-letter cumulative set.

components.title: Spell with Our 19 Sounds
components.intent: Guide students to isolate and speak middle vowel sounds and map sounds to letters using Elkonin boxes for simple words made from the cumulative 19-letter set (e.g., 'cat', 'bug', 'dog', 'lip', 'fan').

finalAssessment.title: Cumulative Letter-Sound Checkup
finalAssessment.intent: Evaluate kindergarten mastery across all 19 letters (Group 1: s, a, t, i, p, n; Group 2: c, k, e, h, r, m, d; Group 3: g, o, u, l, f, b) through child-friendly spoken/tapped sound matching, initial sound recognition, and grapheme-phoneme identification.

cards.title: Gift and Octopus
cards.definition: Letter G says /g/ and letter O says /ŏ/.
cards.timelineContext: You already know sounds like s, a, and t!
cards.originStory: Open your mouth into an O shape to say /ŏ/ like octopus!
cards.curiosityNote: Your throat buzzes softly when you say /g/!
cards.visualPrompt: A cheerful orange octopus holding a colorful gift box with big bubbly letters G and O floating nearby, simple kindergarten style, bright colors.

cards.title: Umbrella and Lion
cards.definition: Letter U says /ŭ/ and letter L says /l/.
cards.timelineContext: Blend u and l with c and p to read the word cup!
cards.originStory: Pretend to pop open an umbrella up high when you say /ŭ/!
cards.curiosityNote: Your tongue taps your top teeth to say /l/!
cards.visualPrompt: A cute cartoon lion smiling under a bright yellow umbrella in gentle raindrops, with big friendly letters U and L, warm kindergarten art style.

cards.title: Fan and Bat
cards.definition: Letter F says /f/ and letter B says /b/.
cards.timelineContext: Now you know nineteen letters to make big fun words!
cards.originStory: Gently bite your bottom lip and blow air to make /f/!
cards.curiosityNote: Your lips pop open fast when you say /b/!
cards.visualPrompt: A friendly little smiling bat holding a spinning toy fan with cool breezes and big block letters F and B, colorful storybook illustration.

data.title: Super Sound Stretchers!
data.description: Get ready to use your big voice to say some fun letter sounds out loud with me!
data.gradeLevel: kindergarten students (ages 5-6) - Use clear language, relatable examples, foundational skills, and engaging visuals. Encourage exploration and basic problem-solving.

problems.question: Which friend's name starts with the /g/ sound?
problems.rationale: Goat begins with the letter 'g', which makes the /g/ sound like in gulp or garden. Fox starts with the /f/ sound, and bear starts with the /b/ sound. By saying each animal's name out loud, we can hear that goat starts with /g/.
problems.teachingNote: Have students place their fingers gently on their throats to feel the hard /g/ sound vibrate deep in their throat when saying 'goat', contrasting it with the lip movement of /b/ or the gentle puff of air for /f/.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /g/ sound in a spoken word
Distinguish the /g/ sound from other Group 3 sounds like /f/ and /b/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which letter makes the /f/ sound like in fish?
problems.rationale: The letter f makes the /f/ sound, which is the starting sound heard in fish. The letter b makes the /b/ sound like in bear, and the letter m makes the /m/ sound like in monkey. Remembering the sound /f/ helps us connect the spoken word fish to the letter f.
problems.teachingNote: Have students gently rest their top teeth on their lower lip and blow air out to feel how the /f/ sound is produced. You can remind them that the curved top of lowercase f looks like a fishing rod.
successCriteria: Identify the letter f as the letter that makes the /f/ sound
Distinguish the letter f from other consonants like b and m
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which animal starts with the letter f sound?
problems.rationale: The word fox begins with the letter f sound, /f/. In comparison, goat starts with the /g/ sound and lion starts with the /l/ sound. Practicing the first sound in fox shows that it matches letter f.
problems.teachingNote: Prompt students to gently touch their top teeth to their lower lip to make the /f/ sound, helping them feel the sound as they say 'fox'.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /f/ sound in spoken words
Apply knowledge of the letter f to select a matching picture
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the same sound as ball?
problems.rationale: Ball and bear both start with the /b/ sound from letter group 3. Sun begins with the review sound /s/, and tiger begins with the review sound /t/. Recognizing the matching beginning sound shows that you know the /b/ sound.
problems.teachingNote: Have students touch their lips together to feel the /b/ sound when saying 'ball' and 'bear', contrasting it with the hissing /s/ sound in 'sun' and tapping /t/ sound in 'tiger'.
successCriteria: Apply knowledge of the Group 3 letter-sound /b/ to match words with the same initial sound
Distinguish new Group 3 initial sounds from previously learned review sounds
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: The frog sits on a ___.
problems.rationale: The word 'log' correctly completes the sentence because frogs rest on logs in nature. The word blends the Group 3 letter sounds /l/, /o/, and /g/. Frogs eat bugs rather than sit on them, and a bus is a vehicle people ride.
problems.teachingNote: Have students sound out each CVC word (/l/-/o/-/g/, /b/-/u/-/g/, /b/-/u/-/s/) using their Group 3 letter sounds before checking which word makes sense in the context of the sentence.
successCriteria: Apply knowledge of Letter-Sound Group 3 (g, o, u, l, f, b) to decode simple words.
Select the correct decodable word to complete a short sentence.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word has the sound you hear in up?
problems.rationale: The word bug has the short /u/ sound in the middle, just like the word up. The words box and log have the short /o/ sound instead. Listening carefully to the middle sound helps tell /u/ and /o/ apart.
problems.teachingNote: Kindergartners frequently confuse short /o/ and short /u/ because the mouth positions feel very similar. Have students look in a mirror or feel their jaw drop slightly wider for /o/ than for /u/.
successCriteria: Distinguish between the short /u/ and short /o/ vowel sounds in spoken words
Identify a word containing the target short /u/ sound
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

coverage.summary: The lesson introduces Group 3 letter-sounds (g, o, u, l, f, b) with clear concept cards and offers practice in letter discrimination, blending, and oral sound production. However, both declared objectives require cumulative coverage of all 19 letters taught to date. Letter identification only tests the 6 new target letters, omitting all 13 review letters, while oral grapheme-to-phoneme production assesses only a fraction of continuous sounds and vowels (f, l, m, s, a, o) because stop consonants are suppressed by content guards. Neither objective meets the full set coverage required to infer mastery.
